What is family based immigration?
Family immigration is the primary basis for legal immigration to the United States. Under current immigration law, US citizens and legal permanent residents can sponsor certain family members for a visa that offers permanent residence through family ties also known as the “green card.”
The Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) of 1965 formally established family ties as the primary way in which people migrate to the United States.
Today, applications for permanent residence through family ties represent approximately 65 percent of legal immigration each year.
What is “chain migration”?
It is the process by which US citizens and green card holders (permanent residents) bring family members to live in the United States.
